# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Every term defined in the book, with the chapter where it is introduced. Terms you met in cell
biology, tissues or general pathology are not repeated here.

| Term | Meaning | Introduced in |
|---|---|---|
| **Acid-fast stain** | A stain that detects organisms with waxy, mycolic-acid walls, which resist the Gram stain | How bacteria are built |
| **Acute infection** | Rapid onset, then either clearance or death of the host | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Aerotolerant anaerobe** | Ferments only, gains nothing from oxygen, but is not harmed by it | How bacteria are built |
| **Antimicrobial resistance** | The ability of a microbe to grow despite a drug that would normally inhibit or kill it | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Antimicrobial stewardship** | Coordinated effort to use antimicrobials only when needed, at the right dose and duration, to limit selection for resistance | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Antisepsis** | Reducing microbes on living tissue, such as skin preparation before a procedure | Detecting and controlling |
| **Archaea** | A domain of prokaryotes distinct from bacteria; none is an established human pathogen | The microbial world |
| **Atypical** | Of bacteria: not detected by the usual stains and culture, either because there is no cell wall or because the organism grows only inside cells | A map of the bacteria |
| **Bacillus (pl. bacilli)** | A rod-shaped bacterium | How bacteria are built |
| **Bacteriophage (phage)** | A virus that infects bacteria | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Binary fission** | Division of one bacterial cell into two | How bacteria are built |
| **Biofilm** | A community of microbes embedded in a shared matrix on a surface | How bacteria are built |
| **Breakpoint** | The drug concentration that separates organisms likely to respond from those that are not | Detecting and controlling |
| **Capsule** | A polysaccharide layer outside the cell wall that resists phagocytosis | How bacteria are built |
| **Carrier** | A person who harbours and can transmit an organism without being ill | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Chocolate agar** | Agar made with heated blood, supplying factors released from lysed red cells for fastidious organisms | A map of the bacteria |
| **Chronic infection** | Infection and inflammation continuing for months or years | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Coccus (pl. cocci)** | A spherical bacterium | How bacteria are built |
| **Colonisation** | Microbes living and multiplying at a site without causing damage | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Colonisation resistance** | Protection given by resident microbes, which occupy sites and consume nutrients that incoming organisms need | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Competent** | Of a bacterium: able to take up DNA from its surroundings | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Conjugation** | Transfer of a plasmid from one bacterium to another through direct contact | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Conjugate vaccine** | A vaccine in which a polysaccharide is linked to a protein to improve the immune response, particularly in young children | Detecting and controlling |
| **Contamination** | Microbes present on a surface without multiplying | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Damage-response framework** | The view that disease is defined by host damage, which may come from the microbe, from the host's response, or from both | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Differential medium** | A medium on which colonies look different according to a metabolic property | Detecting and controlling |
| **Disease** | Damage sufficient to produce signs or symptoms | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Disinfection** | Removing most organisms from an inanimate object; does not reliably kill spores | Detecting and controlling |
| **Domain** | The highest rank of classification: Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya | The microbial world |
| **Doubling time** | The time a bacterial population takes to double in number | How bacteria are built |
| **Efflux pump** | A membrane protein that expels drugs from the cell | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Endemic** | Constantly present in a population at a baseline level | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Endospore (spore)** | A dormant, dehydrated bacterial cell inside protective coats, resistant to heat and chemicals | How bacteria are built |
| **Endotoxin** | Lipopolysaccharide of the Gram-negative outer membrane; its lipid A triggers inflammation | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Enriched medium** | A medium with added nutrients for organisms that cannot make them | Detecting and controlling |
| **Epidemic** | A sharp rise in cases above the endemic baseline | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Epidemic curve** | A plot of cases against time of onset; its shape distinguishes point-source from person-to-person spread | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Eukarya** | The domain of organisms whose cells have a nucleus, including fungi, protozoa, helminths and humans | The microbial world |
| **Exotoxin** | A protein toxin, secreted by bacteria, acting on a specific target | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Facultative anaerobe** | Respires with oxygen when available and ferments without it | How bacteria are built |
| **Fastidious** | Requiring nutrients it cannot make, so needing enriched media | A map of the bacteria |
| **Fermentation** | Making ATP from glycolysis alone, with no electron transport chain | How bacteria are built |
| **Fomite** | An inanimate object that carries organisms between people | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Gastritis** | Inflammation of the stomach lining | The microbial world (case) |
| **Germ theory of disease** | The principle that specific microbes cause specific diseases | The microbial world |
| **Gram stain** | A stain that sorts bacteria by cell envelope: purple (thick peptidoglycan) or pink (thin wall plus outer membrane) | How bacteria are built |
| **Haemolysis** | Destruction of red blood cells; on blood agar, clearing (beta) or green discolouration (alpha) around colonies | Gram-positive cocci |
| **Helminth** | A parasitic worm; a many-celled animal | The microbial world |
| **Herd immunity threshold** | The fraction of a population that must be immune for an outbreak to shrink: 1 − 1/R₀ | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Horizontal gene transfer** | Acquisition of genes from another organism rather than from a parent cell | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Hypotension** | Dangerously low blood pressure | Gram-positive cocci |
| **Incubation period** | Time between infection and the appearance of symptoms | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Infection** | Microbes multiplying in tissue, with a host response | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Infectious period** | The time during which a person can transmit an organism | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Intrinsic resistance** | Resistance that is a property of a whole species | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Koch's postulates** | Four criteria for establishing that a microbe causes a disease | The microbial world |
| **Latent infection** | Persistence of an organism in a silent state, with the possibility of reactivation | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)** | The molecule making up the outer face of the Gram-negative outer membrane; see endotoxin | How bacteria are built |
| **Lysis** | Bursting of a cell | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Lysogenic conversion** | A change in a bacterium's traits caused by genes carried by a prophage | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Lysogenic cycle** | A phage genome integrated into the bacterial chromosome and copied with it | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Lytic cycle** | A phage replicating and bursting its host cell | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **MALDI-TOF** | Mass spectrometry that identifies an organism from the protein profile of a colony | Detecting and controlling |
| **Microaerophile** | Needs oxygen, but is damaged at normal atmospheric levels | How bacteria are built |
| **Microbiota** | The community of microbes that normally lives on and in the body | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Microorganism (microbe)** | A living thing too small to see without a microscope | The microbial world |
| **Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC)** | The lowest drug concentration that prevents visible growth | Detecting and controlling |
| **Molecular mimicry** | Host damage caused by antibodies raised against a microbe cross-reacting with host tissue | Gram-positive cocci |
| **MRSA** | *Staphylococcus aureus* carrying an acquired gene for an altered wall-building protein that binds some drugs poorly | Gram-positive cocci |
| **Mutation** | A change in the DNA sequence, usually a copying error | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Mycolic acid** | The waxy wall component of mycobacteria that resists the Gram stain | How bacteria are built |
| **Nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT)** | A test that copies a target sequence many times until it can be detected | Detecting and controlling |
| **Obligate aerobe** | Can make ATP only with oxygen | How bacteria are built |
| **Obligate anaerobe** | Poisoned by oxygen; grows only where oxygen is absent | How bacteria are built |
| **Obligate intracellular** | Able to grow only inside a living host cell | A map of the bacteria |
| **One Health** | The principle that human, animal and environmental health are interdependent | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Operon** | A group of related bacterial genes transcribed onto one mRNA | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Opportunistic pathogen** | An organism of low virulence that causes disease when defences are impaired or when it reaches a site it does not normally occupy | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Outbreak** | More cases than expected in a place and time | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Pandemic** | An epidemic across many countries | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Pathogen** | A microbe able to cause disease | The microbial world |
| **Pathogenicity island** | A cluster of virulence genes acquired together by horizontal transfer | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Peptic ulcer** | A breach in the lining of the stomach or duodenum | The microbial world (case) |
| **Peptidoglycan** | The mesh of sugar chains and peptides forming the bacterial cell wall | How bacteria are built |
| **Plasmid** | A small circular DNA molecule that replicates independently of the chromosome | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Porin** | A channel in the Gram-negative outer membrane through which small molecules pass | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Prion** | A misfolded host protein that converts normal copies of itself; it has no genome | The microbial world |
| **Prokaryote** | A cell without a nucleus or membrane-bound organelles | The microbial world |
| **Prophage** | A phage genome integrated into a bacterial chromosome | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Protozoan** | A single-celled eukaryotic microbe | The microbial world |
| **Puerperal fever** | Infection following childbirth | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Pyogenic** | Pus-forming | Gram-positive cocci |
| **Reactive oxygen species** | Partly reduced forms of oxygen, such as superoxide and hydrogen peroxide, that damage proteins and DNA | How bacteria are built |
| **Reproduction number (R₀, R)** | R₀: cases generated by one case in a fully susceptible population. R: cases generated under current conditions | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Reservoir** | Where an organism normally lives and multiplies | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Resolution** | The smallest separation at which two points can be distinguished; about 0.2 µm for a light microscope | The microbial world |
| **Selection** | Differential survival and multiplication of variants already present in a population | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Selective medium** | A medium containing agents that suppress unwanted organisms | Detecting and controlling |
| **Serology** | Detection of a patient's antibodies as evidence of exposure | Detecting and controlling |
| **Siderophore** | A molecule that captures iron bound to host proteins | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Sterilisation** | Killing or removing all microbial life, including spores | Detecting and controlling |
| **Strict pathogen** | An organism that causes disease in people with normal defences | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Superantigen** | A toxin that activates a large fraction of T cells at once, causing damaging cytokine release | Gram-positive cocci |
| **Toxigenic** | Producing a toxin | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Toxoid** | An inactivated protein toxin used as a vaccine | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Transduction** | Transfer of bacterial DNA from one cell to another by a phage | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Transformation** | Uptake of free DNA from the surroundings by a competent bacterium | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Transposon** | A DNA segment that can move to a new position, including from chromosome to plasmid | How bacteria copy themselves |
| **Tropism** | The specific tissues or cells an organism can occupy, set largely by the receptor it binds | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Vector** | An arthropod that carries an organism between hosts | Transmission and outbreaks |
| **Virion** | A single virus particle | The microbial world |
| **Virulence factor** | Any microbial product or structure that helps it infect or damage a host | Microbes and their hosts |
| **Whole-genome sequencing** | Reading an organism's entire genome, at a resolution that can link cases in an outbreak | Detecting and controlling |
| **Zoonosis** | An infection transmitted from animals to humans | Transmission and outbreaks |
